issues.description: The problem statement UML and the solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with signature StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template's StockIngredient provides only a four-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch prevents students from using or instantiating StockIngredient as described in the specification and shown in the solution (and as used in the commented examples in Main).
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a three-parameter constructor in the template that matches the UML and the solution: public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity). Alternatively, add an overloaded 3-arg constructor that delegates to the existing 4-arg constructor (e.g., calling this(name, price, quantity, false)). This will align the template with the problem statement and allow students to instantiate StockIngredient as expected.

issues.description: The StockIngredient constructor signature differs between the problem statement / solution and the template. The UML and solution expect a 3-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), and the commented examples in Main instantiate StockIngredient with three arguments. The template's StockIngredient class only exposes a 4-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This API mismatch (constructor parameter difference) breaks the direct mapping from the problem description and example usage to the template implementation and will confuse students when they try to create StockIngredient instances with three arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a 3-argument constructor public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) in the template StockIngredient class (or overload the existing constructor) so it matches the UML/problem statement and the solution. Alternatively, update the problem statement and examples to document the additional boolean parameter if that was intentional.
